threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success criteria, and initial backlog for the program.

messages.text:
Kicking off the Hybrid Workplace Wellbeing and Client Visit Program for project_title: Hybrid Workplace Wellbeing & Client Visit Program.
Goal for this thread: align on scope, success criteria for the first three months, and confirm owners and rough dates for T1–T4.
From the project pack, we have: wellbeing guidelines (T1, linked to A1), client visit playbook (T2, linked to A2), on-site visit checklist (T3), and centralised calendar (T4).
Proposal for initial scope for the first three months:
- Focus on one hybrid office as the main site, with a few external client visits coordinated through the same structure.
- Limit to a small but visible set of wellbeing routines on-site and remote, documented in A1.
- Use the client visit playbook A2 and checklist to standardise at least 10 visits.
Draft success metrics:
- Employee side: at least 60 percent of employees in the pilot office report that the new routines are clear and easy to follow.
- Client side: at least 80 percent of visiting clients rate their on-site experience as good or excellent.
- Operational: no major scheduling conflicts between client visits and wellbeing activities in the shared calendar A4 during the first three months.
For ownership, the project pack already suggests:
- T1 and T5 and T12 with 99128.
- T2 and T7 and T10 with 382239.
- T3 and T4 and T6 and T8 and T9 and T11 with management assistants.
In this thread we need to confirm if we keep that split for T1–T4 and agree on realistic dates within the 21-day deadline.
Can each of you react and suggest any adjustments to scope or metrics before we lock them in under D1 and confirm owners and dates under D2

Thanks for framing this.
On scope: focusing on one hybrid office for the first three months makes sense from a client relationship angle. It lets us refine the visit flow before we scale.
On success metrics, I would suggest we make the client side a bit more specific:
- Target at least 15 client visits following the playbook A2 in the first three months.
- For those visits, aim for 80 percent of feedback forms completed, with at least 80 percent rating the experience as good or excellent.
This ties directly into T2 and T7 and T10 later.
On ownership for T2: I am comfortable taking full ownership, but I will need input from 99128 on the wellbeing aspects and from one of the management assistants on the operational steps.
For dates, if we assume day 0 is today:
- T2 first draft of the playbook by day 7.
- Review and adjustments by day 12.
- Final sign-off by day 15.
Open question: for the employee metric, do we want to measure awareness of the guidelines A1 or actual behaviour change in the first three months

From my side on T1 and the wellbeing guidelines A1, I can work with the proposed scope.
Given the 21-day limit, I suggest we keep the first three months focused on:
- Clear daily routines for on-site days: short movement breaks, basic ergonomic tips, and simple mental health check-in suggestions.
- A lighter section for remote days: posture reminders, screen breaks, and how to use existing tools for short check-ins.
For the employee metric, I would start with awareness and clarity, as suggested. Behaviour change will take longer to measure properly.
On timing for T1:
- Draft guidelines by day 8.
- Share with HR and operations for review by day 10.
- Incorporate feedback and finalise by day 15.
I will need help from a management assistant to make sure the guidelines are available in two languages and uploaded correctly, and to link them in the internal communication plan later.

On T3 and T4 from the management assistant side:
- For T3, I can take the lead on the on-site client visit checklist, with input from 382239 and 99128. I will make sure it covers room setup, safety, refreshments, and materials, and that we have both printed and digital versions aligned with A3.
- For T4, I suggest we use the existing office calendar system and create a shared calendar that mirrors the structure in A4.
Proposed dates:
- T3: first draft checklist by day 6, review with you both by day 9, final by day 12.
- T4: calendar structure proposal by day 5, test events with stakeholders by day 9, finalised by day 11.
On metrics, I like the operational one about no major scheduling conflicts. We could also track how many visits and wellbeing activities are visible in the shared calendar A4 versus how many actually happen, to see if people are using it consistently.
If this works for everyone, we can confirm that:
- T1 owner: 99128.
- T2 owner: 382239.
- T3 owner: 507162.
- T4 owner: 507162.
And we keep the dates above as our initial plan under D2.

I can support on some of the admin parts if needed, especially around uploading documents and sharing links.
One question on T4: do we want separate calendars for client visits and wellbeing activities, or one combined calendar with colour coding as in A4
If we go for one combined calendar, I will need clear naming rules so that reception and managers can quickly see what is what.
Also, for T3, should the checklist A3 include a step for checking any specific health and safety posters or materials in the room, or is that handled elsewhere

Good questions.
On T4: I recommend one combined calendar with clear colour coding and naming conventions, as described in A4. That will reduce the risk of double-booking rooms and people. We can document the naming rules directly in the calendar description and in the internal communication plan later.
On T3 and A3: yes, let us include a simple step to confirm that required health and safety information is visible in the room. The detailed legal content will still be owned by HR and operations, but the checklist can remind assistants to verify that it is present.
I will work with 507162 to define the naming rules and colour codes when we get to T4.
If there are no objections, I suggest we lock in the calendar approach as part of our scope for the first three months.

On the employee metric, I agree with 99128 that we start with awareness and clarity.
Maybe we can phrase it as:
- At least 70 percent of employees in the pilot office confirm they know where to find the guidelines A1 and feel they are clear.
We can add a softer indicator on behaviour, like:
- At least half of respondents say they have tried at least one of the suggested routines.
This keeps expectations realistic for the first three months.
If we align on this, I am comfortable treating this as part of the final scope under D1.

The suggested wording for the employee metric works for me.
For the wellbeing scope, I will keep the first version of A1 simple and practical so that we can reach that awareness target.
I will also make sure that the survey questions in T5 later can capture both awareness and whether people tried at least one routine.
From my side, I am fine to confirm this as part of the scope for the first three months.

I am comfortable owning T3 and T4 with the dates you proposed.
To answer 425046 on the calendar structure: I will set up one combined calendar with two main colour codes, one for client visits and one for wellbeing activities, and a short naming rule like:
- CV - Client name - Visit type.
- WB - Activity name - Target group.
I will document this in the calendar description and share a short note in the channel when T4 is ready.
If everyone agrees, we can treat this as the agreed ownership and timeline for T3 and T4 under D2.

Let us summarise what we have so far so we can close D1 and D2.
Scope for the first three months:
- One hybrid office as the main pilot site.
- Wellbeing routines documented in A1 for on-site and remote days, kept simple and practical.
- Client visit experience standardised via the playbook A2 and checklist A3, targeting at least 15 visits.
Success metrics:
- Employees: at least 70 percent know where to find A1 and find it clear, and at least half report trying one routine.
- Clients: at least 15 visits using A2, with 80 percent of feedback forms completed and 80 percent rating the visit as good or excellent.
- Operations: no major scheduling conflicts in the shared calendar A4, and consistent use of the calendar for visits and wellbeing activities.
Ownership and initial deadlines for T1–T4:
- T1 (wellbeing guidelines A1): owner 99128, draft by day 8, final by day 15.
- T2 (client visit playbook A2): owner 382239, draft by day 7, final by day 15.
- T3 (on-site checklist A3): owner 507162, draft by day 6, final by day 12.
- T4 (centralised calendar A4): owner 507162, structure by day 5, final by day 11.
Unless there are strong objections today, I will record this as our confirmed scope and task ownership under D1 and D2.

The summary looks good to me.
I confirm ownership of T2 with the proposed dates and metrics.
I will coordinate with 99128 and 507162 as soon as I have the first outline of A2 ready.

I am aligned with the scope and metrics as summarised.
I confirm ownership of T1 with the proposed dates and will keep you posted once the first draft of A1 is ready for review.

Confirmed from my side as well.
I will proceed with T3 and T4 according to the plan and share quick updates in this channel when the drafts are ready.

next_steps.when: by day 8 for draft, day 15 for final
by day 7 for draft, day 15 for final
by day 6 for draft, day 12 for final
by day 5 for structure, day 11 for final

threads.thread_goal: Define the client visit playbook and on-site checklist details.

messages.text:
As agreed in TH1, here is the first draft structure for the Client Visit Playbook A2, linked to T2.
Proposed sections:
1. Purpose and scope.
2. Roles and responsibilities for visits.
3. Pre-visit steps.
4. On-site visit flow.
5. Post-visit follow-up.
6. Integration with wellbeing program and calendar.
7. Client segmentation and visit priorities (T7).
Pre-visit steps (section 3):
- Confirm visit objective and attendees.
- Check the central calendar A4 for potential conflicts.
- Reserve room and equipment.
- Coordinate with 507162 on the on-site checklist A3.
- Share a short pre-visit note with the client, including any wellbeing-related information (for example, quiet spaces, accessibility, breaks).
On-site visit flow (section 4):
- Reception welcome using A3.
- Short wellbeing-friendly office tour (highlighting quiet areas, ergonomic workstations, and any wellbeing activities happening that day).
- Main meeting.
- Optional short break with refreshments.
- Closing and next steps.
Post-visit follow-up (section 5):
- Send thank-you email.
- Share any agreed materials.
- Trigger client feedback survey from A5.
- Log visit in CRM and in the monthly status report template A8 later.
I would like feedback from 99128 on the wellbeing touchpoints in sections 3 and 4, and from 507162 and 425046 on how best to align A2 with the on-site checklist A3 and the calendar.
Once we refine the structure, we can move to approval under D3.

Thanks for sharing the structure.
On the wellbeing touchpoints in sections 3 and 4, I suggest we make a few items more explicit:
Pre-visit:
- Ask the client if they have any accessibility needs or preferences for the visit.
- Mention that the office follows the wellbeing guidelines A1, so they know what to expect.
On-site flow:
- During the office tour, include a short explanation of how we support healthy work routines, for example, break areas and ergonomic setups.
- Offer water or other refreshments early in the visit, not only during the optional break.
- If the visit is long, plan a short stretch or movement break.
I can help draft a short script for the wellbeing-friendly tour section in A2, but I will need support from the assistants to make sure it fits with the actual office layout.

From the assistant side, the structure looks workable.
For alignment with A3 and T3, I propose we mirror the same phases:
- Before client arrival.
- Client arrival and welcome.
- During the visit.
- After the visit.
Then A3 can list concrete checks under each phase, while A2 explains the why and the overall flow.
For example:
- Before arrival: room booked, room set up, safety and wellbeing materials visible, refreshments prepared.
- Arrival: reception greeting, sign-in, offer water, explain basic facilities.
- During: follow the tour script, check timing for breaks.
- After: room reset, materials collected, feedback survey triggered.
If we agree on this, I will adjust the T3 checklist draft to match the A2 structure so that we can later lock the final version under D4.

I like the idea of mirroring phases between A2 and A3.
One thing I am not fully clear on: in the on-site flow, who exactly is responsible for checking that the wellbeing-related items are in place in the room Is that reception, the assistant, or the account manager
For T3, it would help to have a simple column for who does what, so that reception staff can follow it without confusion.
Also, should we include a quick reminder in A3 to check if any photos or recordings are planned, so that we can handle consent correctly, or is that covered elsewhere

Good point on responsibilities.
In A2, I will add a short RACI-style overview for the visit phases, but kept simple:
- Reception: first welcome, sign-in, basic directions.
- Management assistant: room setup, materials, refreshments, checking that wellbeing and safety information is visible.
- Account manager: overall visit flow, content of the meeting, and making sure the wellbeing tour and breaks happen.
For T3 and A3, we can add a column for who is responsible for each step, as you suggested.
On photos and recordings: we should include a reminder in both A2 and A3 to check if any photos or recordings are planned and to follow the existing consent process. The detailed legal rules will still need HR or legal confirmation, but at least the checklist can prompt the question.
If 99128 is comfortable with the wellbeing touchpoints and 507162 with the operational flow, I think this structure is close to ready for approval under D3.

The responsibilities and the added wellbeing steps look fine from my side.
I will prepare a short draft for the wellbeing-friendly tour script and share it with you to integrate into A2.
As long as we keep the language simple and consistent with A1, I am comfortable approving the structure of the playbook under D3.

From the operational side, I am also comfortable with the structure.
For T3 and A3, I will:
- Align the phases with A2 as discussed.
- Add a simple responsibility column.
- Include a reminder about photos or recordings and to follow the existing consent process.
Once I have the updated draft, I will share it here for a quick check before we say it is final for the pilot under D4.

Thanks both.
Let me summarise the agreed structure for A2 so we can formally close D3:
1. Purpose and scope.
2. Roles and responsibilities for visits, with a simple overview of who does what.
3. Pre-visit steps, including accessibility questions, calendar A4 checks, room booking, and pre-visit client communication.
4. On-site visit flow, including reception welcome, wellbeing-friendly office tour, refreshments, and planned breaks.
5. Post-visit follow-up, including thank-you email, materials, feedback survey from A5, and logging in CRM and the monthly report A8.
6. Integration with the wellbeing guidelines A1 and the central calendar A4.
7. Client segmentation and visit priorities (T7).
With this, I consider the structure of the client visit playbook approved under D3.
Next, we need to finalise the on-site checklist A3 for pilot use and then lock it under D4.

Here is the updated outline for the on-site client visit checklist A3 under T3, based on our discussion:
Sections:
1. Before client arrival.
2. Client arrival and welcome.
3. During the visit.
4. After the visit.
Examples of checklist items with responsibilities:
Before arrival:
- Room booked and confirmed in calendar A4 (assistant).
- Room set up with seating, screen, and materials (assistant).
- Safety and wellbeing information visible (assistant).
- Refreshments prepared (assistant).
Arrival and welcome:
- Reception greeting and sign-in (reception).
- Offer water and explain basic facilities (reception).
During the visit:
- Follow office tour script from A2, including wellbeing touchpoints (account manager).
- Check timing for breaks and offer refreshments (account manager).
- If photos or recordings are planned, confirm consent according to policy (account manager).
After the visit:
- Room reset and materials collected (assistant).
- Confirm that feedback survey will be sent (account manager).
If 99128 and 382239 are ok with this, I suggest we treat this version of A3 as final for the pilot and lock it under D4.

The checklist outline looks clear and matches the wellbeing aspects we discussed.
I am comfortable using this version of A3 for the pilot.
From my side, we can lock it under D4.

Agreed, the checklist A3 is aligned with the playbook A2 and should work well for the pilot.
I confirm that we can treat this version as final for pilot use under D4.
I will reference A3 directly in the final A2 document so that account managers know which checklist to use.

next_steps.when: this week, to integrate final structure into A2
today, to upload the final A3 template for pilot use

threads.thread_goal: Set up calendar, communication plan, and training session logistics.

messages.text:
As a follow-up to TH1 and TH2, here is a proposal for the calendar setup and launch communications, covering T4, T6, and T8, and referencing A4, A6, and A7.
Calendar structure (T4, A4):
- One combined calendar in our existing office system.
- Colour codes: blue for client visits, green for wellbeing activities.
- Naming convention:
  - CV - Client name - Visit type.
  - WB - Activity name - Target group.
Access rules proposal:
- Read access: all employees in the pilot office.
- Edit access: management assistants and account managers.
- Event owners: whoever creates the event is responsible for keeping it updated.
Internal communication plan (T6, A6):
- Launch email in two languages explaining the program, linking to A1, A2, A3, and the calendar A4.
- Short FAQ for employees and client-facing staff.
- Timeline: teaser one week before launch, main launch message three days before, reminder on launch day.
Training session logistics (T8, A7):
- One 60-minute session for assistants and account managers.
- Agenda: overview of guidelines A1, playbook A2, checklist A3, calendar A4, and surveys A5.
- Speakers: 99128 for wellbeing content, 382239 for client visit flow.
- Proposed date: middle of week 3, so that materials are mostly ready but still before full launch.
We need to choose the final calendar structure and access rules under D5 and confirm the training date, duration, and agenda under D6.
Feedback welcome, especially from 507162 and 425046 on the calendar and comms, and from 99128 and 382239 on the training content.

On the calendar side (T4, A4), the structure and naming convention you propose match what we discussed earlier.
I would only add one detail: for client visits, we should include the main account manager initials at the end of the title, for example, CV - Client name - Intro visit - AM.
This will help assistants quickly see who to contact if something changes.
On access rules, I agree with read access for all and edit access for assistants and account managers.
For the internal communication plan (T6, A6), I can draft the launch email and FAQ in two languages and coordinate with HR and sales to align the timing.
For the training session (T8, A7), the 60-minute slot with 99128 and 382239 as speakers works for me. I suggest we schedule it for the Wednesday of week 3 at 10:00, which usually has fewer client meetings.
If everyone is ok, we can treat this as our final calendar structure and access rules under D5, and the training date and agenda under D6.

I can help with some of the communication tasks.
One question on A6: in the FAQ, should we include a short section for reception and front-desk staff specifically, or is the general FAQ enough
They will be using A3 a lot, so maybe a few examples of typical questions from clients would help.
Also, for the calendar A4, do we want to add a short note in the launch email explaining that not all wellbeing activities are mandatory, to avoid confusion

On the training content (T8, A7), I can cover the wellbeing guidelines A1 and how they connect to the client visit experience.
I suggest the following split for the 60 minutes:
- 10 minutes: program overview and why we are doing this.
- 15 minutes: wellbeing guidelines A1 and how they show up in daily routines.
- 20 minutes: client visit playbook A2 and checklist A3, led by 382239 with my support on wellbeing touchpoints.
- 10 minutes: calendar A4 and how to book visits and activities.
- 5 minutes: Q and A.
I am available on the Wednesday of week 3 at 10:00, so that time works for me.
For A6, I can provide a short paragraph explaining the wellbeing angle for the launch email.

The proposed training split looks good.
I can take the 20-minute section on A2 and A3, focusing on:
- How to prepare for a visit using the playbook.
- How to coordinate with assistants and reception using the checklist.
- How to bring in the wellbeing elements without making the visit feel too formal.
Wednesday of week 3 at 10:00 works for me as well.
On the calendar A4, I support the combined structure and the access rules that 507162 proposed.
From my side, we can confirm D5 and D6 once we capture the final wording.

On the open questions from 425046:
- For A6, I agree we should add a short section in the FAQ specifically for reception and front-desk staff, with 2–3 typical client questions and suggested answers.
- In the launch email, we can add one sentence clarifying that wellbeing activities in the calendar A4 are mostly optional unless marked otherwise.
Let me summarise the calendar and training decisions so we can close D5 and D6:
Calendar (T4, A4):
- One combined calendar in the existing system.
- Colour codes: blue for client visits, green for wellbeing activities.
- Naming convention: CV - Client name - Visit type - AM initials; WB - Activity name - Target group.
- Read access for all employees in the pilot office; edit access for management assistants and account managers.
Training (T8, A7):
- 60-minute session on Wednesday of week 3 at 10:00.
- Agenda: program overview, A1, A2, A3, A4, and surveys A5, plus Q and A.
- Speakers: 99128 and 382239.
Unless there are objections today, I will record this as our final calendar structure and access rules under D5 and the confirmed training date and agenda under D6.

No objections from my side.
I will:
- Finalise the calendar A4 with the agreed structure and access rules.
- Draft the launch email and FAQ A6, including a short section for reception and a note about optional wellbeing activities.
- Send calendar invites for the training session A7 on the Wednesday of week 3 at 10:00.
We can consider D5 and D6 confirmed.

Confirmed from my side as well.
The calendar setup and training plan are clear and workable.
I will make sure the final A2 references the calendar A4 and the training A7 so that account managers know where to look.

next_steps.when: this week, to finalise calendar A4 and access rules
by early next week, to send draft A6 for review
today, to send training invite and update A7

threads.thread_goal: Agree on survey templates, compliance checks, and reporting format.

messages.text:
Starting the thread on surveys, compliance, and reporting, covering T5, T9, T11, and T12, and referencing A5 and A8.
Draft survey approach (T5, A5):
- Two short surveys: one for employees, one for clients.
- Both available in two languages.
Employee survey focus:
- Awareness of the wellbeing guidelines A1.
- Clarity and usefulness of the routines.
- Whether they have tried at least one routine.
- Open question for suggestions.
Client survey focus:
- Overall visit experience.
- Clarity and friendliness of the visit flow.
- Perception of the office environment and wellbeing aspects.
- Likelihood to visit again or recommend.
Compliance and approvals (T11):
- I propose that we send the draft surveys and the wellbeing guidelines A1 to HR and legal for review.
- Once feedback is received, we update the documents and mark the final versions as approved in the shared drive.
Reporting and improvement (T9, T12, A8):
- Monthly status report template A8 to include: number of visits and wellbeing activities, attendance, key issues, and key feedback themes.
- Continuous improvement process: collect feedback from surveys and from a short monthly check-in, prioritise 1–2 changes, and document them.
I would appreciate input from 548231 and 507162 on the reporting template A8 and from 382239 on the client survey questions.
We also need to agree on the review cadence for the improvement process and then approve the final survey templates under D7 and the reporting template and cadence under D8.

On the client survey (T5, A5), I suggest we keep it very short to maximise response rates.
Possible structure:
- 1 question on overall satisfaction with the visit (for example, a 1–5 scale).
- 1 question on how welcome and comfortable they felt in the office.
- 1 question on how clear the visit agenda and next steps were.
- 1 question on whether the environment supported a productive meeting (lighting, noise, comfort).
- Optional open comment.
We can add a final question on likelihood to visit again or recommend, but we should avoid making it feel like a long marketing survey.
For reporting A8, I can help define a simple section for client-related insights, such as:
- Number of client visits.
- Average satisfaction score.
- Top 2–3 themes from comments.
This will make it easier to connect the program to client relationship outcomes.

On the reporting template A8 (T9), I propose the following sections:
1. Overview.
- Summary of key activities this month (number of visits and wellbeing sessions).
2. Attendance.
- Attendance rates for wellbeing activities.
- Number of client visits completed.
3. Feedback.
- Employee survey highlights.
- Client survey highlights.
4. Issues and risks.
- Any scheduling conflicts or operational issues.
- Any compliance or safety concerns raised.
5. Actions.
- 1–2 concrete improvements planned for next month.
For the continuous improvement process (T12), we can set a monthly review cadence for the pilot office, with a slightly more detailed quarterly review once we scale.
On T11, I suggest that 507162 sends A1 and the survey drafts A5 to HR and legal, and then posts their feedback and approval status in this channel.
If we align on this, we can move towards approving the survey templates under D7 and the reporting template and cadence under D8.

I can take care of T11 from the assistant side.
Plan:
- Once 99128 finalises the draft surveys in A5 and the wellbeing guidelines A1, I will send them to HR and legal with a short note explaining the program.
- I will track their feedback and update the approval status in the shared drive.
- I will then post a short summary here confirming which documents are approved.
On A8 and T9, the sections you propose look clear. I can set up the template in our shared folder and add one example report for the pilot month.
For the review cadence (T12), a monthly review for the pilot office plus a quarterly summary sounds reasonable to me.

I have one question on the employee survey.
Do we want to ask about specific wellbeing activities they attended, or just whether they joined any activity at all
If we list specific activities, the survey might need to change more often, but it could give more detail for A8.
Also, for the monthly review, who will be in the meeting Is it only the pilot office team, or do we include HR as well

On the employee survey, I would keep it simple for now:
- Ask whether they joined any wellbeing activity in the last quarter.
- Provide an open text field where they can mention which activity they joined and what worked well or not.
This way we do not need to update the survey every time we add a new activity, but we still get some detail for A8.
For the monthly review meeting, I suggest we keep it small for the pilot:
- One representative from the pilot office management.
- One management assistant.
- Myself.
We can invite HR when there are specific topics that need their input, and we can share the monthly A8 summary with them.
If everyone is ok with this, I will adjust the T5 drafts accordingly.

The simplified client survey structure works for me.
To connect it to our earlier metrics, we can:
- Use the overall satisfaction question as the main score.
- Use the comfort and environment questions to track the impact of the wellbeing aspects.
- Use the open comment to capture anything we did not think of.
As long as HR and legal are comfortable with the wording, I am ready to approve the client survey template under D7.

Let me summarise the survey and reporting setup so we can close D7 and D8.
Surveys (T5, A5):
- Two templates: employees and clients, both in two languages.
- Employee survey: awareness and clarity of A1, whether they tried at least one routine, whether they joined any wellbeing activity, and open comments.
- Client survey: overall satisfaction, feeling of welcome and comfort, clarity of agenda and next steps, environment support for a productive meeting, and optional open comment.
Compliance (T11):
- 507162 will send A1 and the survey drafts A5 to HR and legal, track feedback, and confirm approval status in the channel.
Reporting and improvement (T9, T12, A8):
- Monthly status report A8 with sections on overview, attendance, feedback, issues and risks, and actions.
- Monthly review meeting for the pilot office with a small group, plus a quarterly summary once we scale.
If there are no objections, I will record the survey templates as approved under D7 and the reporting template and review cadence under D8, subject to HR and legal sign-off for wording.

No objections from me.
I will proceed with:
- Finalising the survey templates in A5 based on 99128 and 382239 input.
- Sending A1 and A5 to HR and legal for review under T11.
- Setting up the A8 template and creating an example report for the pilot month under T9.
We can treat D7 and D8 as confirmed, pending the formal HR and legal approval step.

Aligned from my side.
I will finalise the survey questions and the continuous improvement description for T12, and then work with 507162 to send everything for HR and legal review.
Once we have their feedback, I will adjust the documents if needed and confirm that the process is ready for launch.

next_steps.when: this week, to finalise survey questions in A5
after T5 is ready, to send A1 and A5 to HR and legal
before the end of the pilot month, to complete example A8 report
this week, to document the continuous improvement process

threads.thread_goal: Run pilot debrief and decide adjustments before wider rollout.

messages.text:
Pilot debrief for the Hybrid Workplace Wellbeing and Client Visit Program in the pilot office, covering T10 and referencing A1, A2, A3, A5, and A8.
Summary of pilot activities (T10):
- Client visits: 4 visits completed using the playbook A2 and checklist A3.
- Wellbeing activities: 2 on-site sessions and 1 remote session aligned with A1.
- Surveys: client feedback collected for 3 of the 4 visits, employee survey sent once.
Key observations from client visits:
- Clients appreciated the clear structure of the visit and the office tour.
- The wellbeing elements (breaks, refreshments, mention of quiet areas) were noticed but not always used.
- One visit had a minor timing issue due to a room change, but the calendar A4 helped us adjust quickly.
Survey highlights (A5, A8):
- Client satisfaction: average 4.6 out of 5 across the 3 responses.
- Clients rated the welcome and comfort highly; one comment mentioned that the visit felt well organised and relaxed.
- Employee feedback: most respondents know where to find A1 and find it clear; a few asked for more concrete examples for remote days.
Open questions for this thread:
- Do we keep the current scope and success metrics for the first three months as defined under D1, or do we need adjustments based on the pilot
- Is the on-site checklist A3 working as is, or do we need changes before we lock it for wider use under D4
Looking forward to input from 99128 and the assistants on what worked and what needs to change before we roll out more broadly.

From the wellbeing side, a few reflections:
- The on-site activities were well attended, but the remote session had lower participation.
- Employees understood the basic routines in A1, but some asked for more specific examples for remote work, such as how to structure breaks during long online meetings.
